title: Made without a flaw, so come back to the flawless One
subtitle: Al-Bari': the Maker who brings each creature out distinct and free of defect
intro: Al-Bari' (الْبَارِئُ) means the Maker who brings creatures into existence distinct from one another, in balance, and free of any flaw in His work. Nothing He makes is botched or out of place. For you it means this: when you have drifted toward broken things, the way back is to the One who makes nothing broken.

root.sense: The root means to be clear of something and separate from it. Bari' in everyday Arabic is someone innocent, cleared of a charge, and bur' is recovering from an illness. So Al-Bari' brings creatures out separated one from another, each clear of defect and disorder.

row.title: I am too broken to return
sub: He must be done with me

row.title: Return to the Flawless
sub: the Maker of all calls back

knowing: Al-Bari' sits between Al-Khaliq and Al-Musawwir in 59:24. If Al-Khaliq speaks of planning and bringing into being, {idea}Al-Bari' speaks of bringing creatures out cleanly, each separate and sound{/idea}. A human maker can design something well and still produce it badly, with faults in the material or slips in the assembly. With Allah there is no gap between plan and result.

Look at how each kind is kept apart. A tree is a tree, a bird is a bird, a human is a human. Within every kind there is order and balance. The Quran invites you to look at the sky again and again and see whether you can find a single break; your eyes will come back tired, having found none (67:3-4). That flawlessness is the signature of Al-Bari'.

Scholars also link the name to the earth, from which He brought out humankind (11:61), since bara is a word for soil. Either way, the meaning is the same: He brings out what He creates, sound and distinct, and {reward}nothing leaves His hands defective{/reward}.
seeing: The name Bari' appears outside 59:24 in one striking scene. The Children of Israel had taken a golden calf to worship. Musa told them they had wronged themselves, and to turn in repentance to their Bari' (2:54). Of all His names, why this one? A calf is a creature full of limits and weakness. {trap}They had left the One who makes without flaw for a thing that was all flaw{/trap}. So the call was: make a U-turn, back to the Maker who makes no mistakes.
The same verse ends by saying He accepted their repentance. Even after one of the worst betrayals in their history, the door to Al-Bari' was open.
trusting: We all build little calves: a career, a person, a number in the bank, an image of ourselves online. We give them our hope and our fear, and they keep failing us, because they are made things with cracks in them. Knowing Al-Bari' lets you take your heart back from them. {idea}Only the One who makes without flaw can carry the full weight of your trust{/idea}.

It also helps with the shame of failure. You may feel you are the flawed one, the badly made one. Your sins are yours, but your making was not careless. The Maker who shaped you without mistake still calls you back by this very name, the way He called back the people of the calf.
loving: There is relief in loving something that will never let you down. Every human love comes with its cracks. Al-Bari' has none. {reward}The heart rests when it finally turns to the One whose work, and whose care, has no defect at all{/reward}.
now: You have spent another evening refreshing a page, waiting for a message from someone who keeps letting you down. You know it is a cracked thing, and still you lean on it. Close the app and say: I am turning back to my Bari'. The one you were waiting on is a creature; the One you return to has never made a mistake.
old: When I have gone far wrong, I feel I have lost the right to come back.
new: When I have gone far wrong, Al-Bari' calls me back to Himself, the only One without a flaw.
try: Name one thing you have been relying on more than Allah, and today make a small, deliberate U-turn: a sincere repentance and two rak'ahs.

dua.text: Ya Bari', You brought me out of nothing without any fault in Your making. I have leaned on cracked things. I return to You; accept my repentance.
dua.note: Call Him by this name when you repent, as Musa directed his people in 2:54 to turn back to their Bari'.

pairs.why: Al-Khaliq plans and brings into being; Al-Bari' makes sure what comes out is distinct, balanced and flawless.
Once Al-Bari' brings a creature out sound, Al-Musawwir gives it its particular form and face.
The call to return to Al-Bari' in 2:54 ends with His acceptance of repentance.

faq.a: Al-Bari' means the Maker who brings creatures into existence distinct from each other and free of flaw. The root carries the sense of being clear and separate, so His creating is clean, balanced and without defect.

faq.q: Where does Al-Bari' appear in the Quran?
faq.a: As a name with the definite article it appears in 59:24, together with Al-Khaliq and Al-Musawwir. The word also appears twice in 2:54, where Musa tells his people to repent to their Bari' after they worshipped the calf.

faq.q: What is the difference between Al-Khaliq and Al-Bari'?
faq.a: Al-Khaliq highlights measuring and bringing into being. Al-Bari' highlights bringing creatures out separated from one another and free of defect. Scholars describe them, with Al-Musawwir, as stages of one perfect act of creation.
